summary_html: A **court reverses or vacates** a CPS or agency decision due to procedural error, insufficient evidence, or constitutional violation. Federal review data (CFSR, ASFA) tracks judicial determinations on reasonable efforts and due process.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — judicial findings of 'reasonable efforts' compliance  
- **CFSR Regulations (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of judicial/agency conformity  
- **42 U.S.C. § 1983** — civil-rights remedy for unconstitutional removals (14th & 4th Amendments).

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In re A.O. & I.O., Juveniles & In re B.G. & E.G., Juveniles
key_cases.holding: The CHINS merits and disposition orders for four children were reversed and vacated as unsupported by the findings or the record, and the orders allowing a party's advocate to inspect the other children's juvenile records without a need-to-know designation were reversed.
key_cases.relevance: A.O. & I.O. is a recent, published reversal of both the agency-sought adjudication and the resulting disposition.
key_cases.quote: We therefore reverse the CHINS merits determination as unsupported by the findings or the record.

key_cases.holding: The CHINS determination was reversed because the evidence did not support the ground the State pleaded, and the Court declined to reach the disposition order transferring custody to DCF.
key_cases.relevance: This is a published reversal of an agency-sought CHINS adjudication for insufficient evidence.
key_cases.quote: For these reasons, we reverse the family division's determination that J.N. was CHINS.

key_cases.holding: The Human Services Board's reversal of a registry substantiation was itself reversed and remanded because the Board must apply the same substantiation standard DCF applies under its Policy No. 55 rather than a different standard of its own.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Supreme Court reversing an administrative reversal of DCF, showing review runs in both directions.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the Board should have used the standard embodied in Policy No. 55 and must do so on remand

key_cases.holding: Summary judgment applying collateral estoppel to a registry substantiation was reversed because the Human Services Board could not inspect the related CHINS file without a need-to-know designation from the family court under 33 V.S.A. § 5117(b)(1)(F), and the stipulated facts did not establish what the substantiation required.
key_cases.relevance: The decision reverses an administrative ruling that had foreclosed a parent's challenge to DCF.
key_cases.quote: A need-to-know designation from the family court was required before the Board could inspect the contents of the juvenile files in question.

key_cases.case_name: In re L.H., L.H. and L.H., Juveniles
key_cases.holding: Termination orders were reversed and remanded for a new hearing because the lawyer who had represented the children then represented the State in the same matter, creating an unwaived conflict of interest that prejudiced the parents.
key_cases.relevance: It is the leading Vermont example of a court vacating a termination outcome for a structural fairness defect rather than for evidentiary insufficiency.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that a conflict of interest by the State's counsel compromised the proceedings

state_agency.name: Vermont Department for Children and Families, Family Services Division

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Date the administrative reviewer sent notice of the decision on the substantiation review (33 V.S.A. § 4916a(i)); the review itself must be requested within 30 days after the Department sent notice of the right to review (33 V.S.A. § 4916a(c)(1))
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: If no review by the Human Services Board is requested, the Department's decision is final and the person has no further right of review under this section; the Board may grant a waiver upon good cause shown (33 V.S.A. § 4916b(d)).
